text.p: Wayne Ferreira of South Africa, the defending champion and 13th seed at the $2.3 million Canadian Open, advanced to the second round with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-1 victory over Daniel Vacek of the Czech Republic Monday.

After failing to convert three set points ahead 5-4, 40-love in the opening set, the 28th-ranked Ferreira took the tiebreaker with a winning backhand passing shot and then had little trouble with the 61st-ranked Vacek the rest of the way.
Petr Korda of the Czech Republic, the ninth seed in the 56-player draw which awards first-round byes to the top eight seeds, was beaten 6-4 6-4 by American Justin Gimelstob.
Another upset victim was 10th-seeded Tim Henman of Britain. He lost 7-6 (7-3) 4-6 6-3 to Canadian wild card entry Sebastien LeBlanc, ranked 885th.
Two other seeded players moving into the second round were 12th-seeded Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden and 16th-seeded Jan Siemerink of the Netherlands.
The 25-year-old Ferreira served well and played consistently from the backcourt to record his ninth win in a row over Vacek.

An 80-minute rain delay at 7-6 4-1, 30-40 on Vacek's serve in the second set did not help the Czech. "You never know what can happen after a rain delay, but I played two good points to break him so it turned out to be good for me," said Ferreira.
Talking about his success against Vacek, he added: "I hold my serve pretty easily against him and he struggles to hold his. That can begin to wear on you mentally."

At 20, the 100th-ranked Gimelstob is now the youngest American player in the top 100. Against Korda, the tall righthander took to the net at every opportunity as he overcame a 1-4 first-set deficit to beat the 16th-ranked Korda.

After defeating his compatriot Andre Agassi last week at the ATP Tour event in Los Angeles only to lose in the second round to Byron Black of Zimbabwe, Gimelstob is hoping he has learned a lesson. "If I want to be a good player, I've got to put the good wins back to back," he said.
"Sometimes after a good win I tend to get uptight. But I don't want that to happen this time."
Gimelstob next plays 63rd-ranked Scott Draper of Australia, a 4-6 6-1 6-2 winner over France's Thierry Champion.
LeBlanc took advantage of an off-form Henman to score the best win of his career.
The 23-year-old LeBlanc played serve-and-volley tennis to surprise the 18th-ranked Henman.
Bjorkman, ranked number 24, downed another Canadian wild card, 363rd-ranked Bobby Kokavec, 6-3 6-2.
Rising German star Tommy Haas, ranked 74th, used several timely lobs to wear down the 129th-ranked Canadian Daniel Nestor 5-7 6-4 6-4.
American Jonathan Stark, playing his first match since getting married last week, overcame Armenian Sargis Sargisian 6-7 (3-7) 6-3 6-3.
An all-South African matchup resulted in Marcos Ondruska scoring a 4-6 7-5 6-2 victory over Grant Stafford.

Seeded players scheduled to see action on Tuesday include number four Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia and number eight Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands. American Michael Chang, the top seed, will begin play on Wednesday.
